card.flavorText: Britain made some huge technological advances during WWII, some that would have a great impact on civilian life after the war. The “Bombe” was an electromechanical device developed in 1939 by Alan Turing and a team of scientists at Bletchley Park. The “Bombe” was used to speed up the cracking of Enigma code. In 1943 the British codebreakers developed Colossus, the world's first electronic digital programmable computer. The British would also perfect radar technology, which helped them to detect incoming air raids during the Battle of Britain in 1940. Further development in radar technology led to the invention of the H2S radar, the first airborne radar used to aid bomb targeting. Other British military inventions during WWII was the bouncing bomb, the high-explosive squash head, also known as "high explosive plastic" and the Bailey Bridge, a portable truss bridge that was used by Allied military engineers.
